meta.title: Blade & Brick | Barbers on Lower Clapton Road, E5
meta.description: Two-chair barbershop under the railway bridge on Lower Clapton Road. Skin fades, beard trims, hot towel shaves. Walk-ins welcome. Open Tuesday to Saturday.

rationale: The page is set as a local bulletin: white paper, black ink, one brick-red spot colour that nods to the shop's name. Ruled price ledger, hours table and pull quote make it dense and trustworthy. The loud, chatty side comes through in a marquee, a giant 8pm for Thursday late opening, a circled line and a custom drawing of the railway arch with its two chairs.

props.title: Kemi runs the shop
paragraphs: Kemi runs Blade & Brick from under the railway bridge on Lower Clapton Road. There are two chairs, so it is never a big room, and that is how the talk gets going.

The music is loud. The chat covers football, music, work, whatever the next person brings in with them. The cuts are the part we take seriously: clean skin fades, beards shaped to the face, and a hot towel shave when you want to sit back for a while.
On Saturdays the kids come in for their cuts. On Thursdays we stay open until 8pm for anyone who cannot get here before work.
props.pullQuote: Two chairs is enough to know everyone who sits in them.

quotes.text: Best fade I have had in Hackney. Kemi does not rush it, and the chat is half the reason I come back.
Brought my son in on a Saturday. He sat still the whole time, which has never happened before.
